focus.jtag: S&P closed above 7,700 for the first time, oil kept sliding on Iran deal hopes, futures green again — but 10Y near 1.5-yr high and NFP Friday
focus.jnote: The friendly, record-setting tape carried into Wednesday. Tuesday saw a broad, beyond-Big-Tech rally — the S&P closed +1.79% at ~7,736.52, above 7,700 for the first time ever, and the Dow set another record — as oil kept sliding on optimism that a U.S.–Iran interim deal could reopen the Strait of Hormuz. S&P futures are up ~0.4%, the VIX is low near 16.5, and gold is firm around $4,226. The catch: the 10-year yield remains near a ~1.5-year high (~4.63%) with the Fed hawkish into July payrolls Friday, and a huge Q2 earnings flood keeps single-name gap risk live — the scanner boarded 12 Type A post-earnings gaps this morning (ANET, LLY, KTOS, FLUT and more), but most confirmed on almost no volume with liquidity unverified. Validate every one at the open.
focus.notdown: AI/data-center (ANET +13% after a beat-and-raise) and pharma (LLY +5% on a GLP-1 blowout and raised guidance) are today's cleanest bids. ANET topped Q2 and guided Q3 well above consensus; Lilly beat big and lifted its full-year sales target to $85–87B. Both are boarded bullish Type A gaps — but relative volume was near zero pre-open and options liquidity is UNVERIFIED, so confirm the gap holds and the chain is tradable at 9:35 before selling any bull put.
focus.notup: VPG (−26% on a −79% EPS miss) and FLUT (−7% on a −21% EPS miss) are the boarded bearish gaps. The lean is down, but selling bear calls into a risk-on, record-setting tape carries squeeze risk on any friendly headline — and VPG has NO S/R layers between price and the short strike plus thin (40) open interest. Treat these as half-size-at-most and only if they fail the 9:35 validation on the downside.
focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? Composite eased to 37 (MILD) and P(≥1% gap) is ~29% (below the 35% trigger), which clears the numeric GREEN locks. But two things hold it at YELLOW: (1) the macro backdrop is still tense — the 10Y is near a ~1.5-year high, the Fed is hawkish, and NFP lands Friday; and (2) nearly every one of the 12 boarded names confirmed on near-zero relative volume (0.00–0.71x, all below the 1.3x bar) with ATM spreads unverified (TastyTrade was unreachable) and several with thin open interest. Half size, A-grade only, and validate every candidate at 9:35 ET.

risks: NFP · Fri 8/7 — July payrolls are the week's headliner. A hot print pushes yields higher; a weak one boosts cut hopes — either way, the single-biggest scheduled gap risk this week. Keep every spread's DTE clear of it.
10-year yield near a ~1.5-year high — the 10Y sits around 4.63% with the Fed talking tough. Any further rate pop pressures long-duration tech even on a risk-on tape.

Earnings-cluster gap risk — 12 names boarded today and DIS/SHOP/KMB report next; nearly every boarded gap confirmed on near-zero volume with UNVERIFIED liquidity. Confirm each chain is real and tradable at 9:35 before selling anything.

Thin-liquidity boarded names — ECG (OI 13), KMT (40), VPG (40), KTOS (85) and BWA (280) are below the 500-OI bar; VPG also has NO overhead S/R and IV ~161%. Several may be untradeable in practice — do not force a fill.
Iran / Hormuz talks — an interim deal could land soon, but nothing is signed. A breakdown or any Strait disruption sends crude and the whole tape gapping — the week's biggest tail.

earnings.intro: Q2 season is in one of its busiest stretches — Arista and Eli Lilly already beat this morning, with Disney, Shopify and Kimberly-Clark reporting today, then more mid-week. With the market risk-on but rates high and NFP looming Friday, a single-stock earnings gap on top of macro is a double catalyst — keep every spread clear of its name's print. All 12 boarded Type A names have their NEXT earnings dates ~63–64 days out, well outside a normal DTE.
